A capital-loss balance is not a tax refund: chart the gains and the eligible years

Four editable charts reconcile same-year loss use, a chosen carryback allocation, eligible prior gains and the loss record left for future years.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 5 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Reconcile a hypothetical 2025 capital-loss record across eligible years

Interactive planning lab

2025 net capital-loss record before carryback$9,000
Illustrative allocation to eligible prior gains$7,000
Unapplied record remaining for carryforward$2,000

Original hypothetical historical 2025 example for ordinary eligible capital property, one loss vintage and no other adjustments. All entered losses are already allowable amounts and gains are already taxable amounts on a matching inclusion-rate basis; no inclusion factor is applied again. Same-year use comes first. A separately requested total limits carryback allocation, then the model visits 2022, 2023 and 2024 in that authored order, capped by each entered available gain and the remaining loss. This destination-year ordering is an illustration, not a legal priority or tax-optimization result. Available prior gains and loss eligibility are assumed verified independently. No tax refund, bank receipt, assessment, tax bracket, benefit adjustment, future-year deduction or interest is computed. Earlier loss vintages, inclusion-rate conversion, pre-1985 special rules, business investment losses, listed personal property, denied losses and superficial-loss testing are excluded.

On this page

  1. Identify the loss type and its measurement basis first
  2. Use the same-year loss once before allocating it elsewhere
  3. Give each eligible destination year its own gain capacity
  4. A remaining record and an unfilled request have different meanings
  5. Build any tax and cash estimate separately from the deduction ledger
  6. Sources and scope

The central idea

Track the eligible loss once, identify which gains can absorb it and keep any refund estimate and receipt date in a separate cash plan.

01

Identify the loss type and its measurement basis first

A statement showing an investment loss does not by itself identify an amount available for a tax deduction. This article uses an explicitly historical 2025 example of eligible ordinary capital losses, with all amounts already converted to the appropriate allowable-loss and taxable-gain basis.

CRA’s capital-loss guidance describes same-year netting before a net capital loss is carried to another eligible year. It also distinguishes loss categories and circumstances that require different treatment.

The tool assumes eligibility has been verified separately. It does not establish whether a loss is denied, superficial or subject to special rules. A loss that cannot be claimed must not be inserted simply because a holding declined in value.

Because the inputs are already allowable or taxable amounts, applying another inclusion percentage would reduce them a second time. Historical inclusion-rate adjustments and multiple loss vintages need a fuller record than this one-vintage illustration.

02

Use the same-year loss once before allocating it elsewhere

The original example enters CAD 12,000 of 2025 allowable capital losses and CAD 3,000 of 2025 taxable capital gains before that loss use. Same-year use is the smaller amount, CAD 3,000. The remaining net capital-loss record is CAD 9,000.

The first waterfall shows that bridge. Allocating the full CAD 12,000 again to another year would reuse the CAD 3,000 already absorbed in 2025. The carryback calculation therefore starts with CAD 9,000.

If instead the entered 2025 taxable gain exceeds the allowable loss, the loss is fully used in that year and no negative carryover record appears. For example, CAD 2,000 of allowable loss against CAD 3,000 of taxable gain leaves CAD 1,000 of gain and zero loss to allocate elsewhere.

These are loss-record identities. They do not subtract investment sale losses from the household bank account or calculate a change in tax payable. Any cash from an actual investment sale belongs in its own transaction ledger.

03

Give each eligible destination year its own gain capacity

For a 2025 net capital loss, CRA identifies 2022, 2023 and 2024 as the three previous eligible years and allows the taxpayer to choose destination years. The example assumes independently verified available taxable capital gains of CAD 2,000, CAD 4,000 and CAD 1,000 respectively.

The default requested carryback allocation is CAD 7,000. For transparency, this tool visits the destination years in chronological order: first 2022, then 2023, then 2024. It uses CAD 2,000, CAD 4,000 and CAD 1,000, stopping at each year’s entered capacity.

This ordering is an authored convention. It is not a rule requiring the earliest destination year or evidence that the allocation gives the largest tax saving. Actual year choices require their own assessment of the complete records and consequences.

Do not confuse destination-year choice with the order of loss vintages. CRA’s other-years guidance separately addresses using older loss vintages before newer ones, record keeping and inclusion-rate adjustments. This model contains only the 2025 vintage.

04

A remaining record and an unfilled request have different meanings

After the default CAD 7,000 allocation, CAD 2,000 of the CAD 9,000 net capital-loss record remains unapplied. The second waterfall preserves that remainder as a carryforward record. It is not CAD 2,000 available to pay a household bill today.

Reduce the requested carryback amount to CAD 3,000. Under the declared order, CAD 2,000 is allocated to 2022 and CAD 1,000 to 2023. The remaining record becomes CAD 6,000. Increasing the request again can use more of that record only while eligible gain capacity remains.

Requesting CAD 20,000 at the default gain capacities still allocates only CAD 7,000. A larger request cannot create another eligible gain or another loss. Likewise, entering zero prior-year gain capacity leaves the net loss unapplied even when the requested allocation is large.

The matrix changes the 2025 allowable loss and taxable gain while retaining those other conditions. A larger residual can reflect a larger loss, less same-year use or a limit on carryback capacity. It is a record to reconcile, rather than a standalone measure of financial improvement.

05

Build any tax and cash estimate separately from the deduction ledger

A complete tax calculation is needed to translate an allowed deduction into its effect on tax payable. Assessments, prior payments and the treatment of the full return also affect whether money is refunded. The four charts therefore do not label a loss deduction as a refund.

CRA’s guidance distinguishes taxable-income effects from net-income effects when applying net capital losses across years. The tool does not calculate income-tested benefits, credits or their changes from those different income measures.

The statutory context is Income Tax Act section 111. The official consolidation reviewed here is current to 30 September 2026; the CRA pages address the 2025 return. This dated example is not a determination for a new transaction or a later tax year.

For a practical review, keep the verified loss vintage, matching inclusion basis, gain capacity, chosen applications and remaining record together. Then put any separately supported refund amount and receipt date into the household cash calendar. Until that cash is supported, an unapplied loss balance should not be counted again as money assigned to spending.
